part: Operations matrix with a SIXTH region column: "regions beyond five scroll inside the card"
artboards: 08-operations-redesign-2026-09-08 (which draws five columns and a `SCROLL →` hint)
source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/screens/08-operations-list-redesign-2026-09-08.png (the operator's replacement artboard), plus his /operations STOP SHIP message of 2026-09-09 quoted verbatim in the notes.
notes: OPERATOR, 2026-09-09, item 4, verbatim: "First column sticky; regions beyond five scroll inside the card."

WHY THIS NEEDED ITS OWN MOUNT. Every other matrix mount carries the artboard's five columns, so none of them can tell a table that scrolls at six from one that never scrolls at all. [CONFIRMED 2026-09-09, by measurement] the base this lane started from did NOT scroll at six: with a 96px column floor, six columns summed to 180 + 576 = 756px inside a 1024px scroller on the composed page, so they simply stretched. The floor is now 142px, chosen as the only value where five columns still FIT (180 + 710 = 890px, inside both the 1024px composed scroller and the 892px component-mount scroller) and six do NOT (180 + 852 = 1032px, outside both). Both halves are measured in .discipline/rendering/smoke/ops-matrix-acceptance-smoke.mjs leg E; this spec pins the shape.

The scroll hint in the card head is drawn only when there is somewhere to scroll to, which is why it appears here and not on the five-column mounts: telling a reader to scroll a table that does not move is a false affordance.

children.name: the header hint gains `scroll →` once there IS somewhere to scroll (operator's delete list: the old `click a dimension to open its facts` becomes `N regions · scroll →`)
FIRST COLUMN STICKY still, which is what makes the panning readable rather than merely possible: the row label stays on screen at every scroll offset
the region column floor is the measured 142px, so the sixth column is the one that pushes the table past its scroller
the card still clips, so the scrolled table never paints over its rounded corners
and the card's height is unchanged by the sixth column: the panel slot is still the fixed-height box that holds it

forbid.name: the sixth column does not make a cell wrap into a second line
forbid.reason: The 40px row is the operator's first clause and the column floor is what protects it. Before the floors existed, a table with no minimum width CRUSHED rather than scrolled: the rendering guard measured the dimension column at 21px, wrapping `Regional resource availability` over twelve one-character lines. A doubled row height is that failure returning.
